newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper rallies on U.S. cold, arbitrage option.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper rallies on U.S. cold, arbitrage option.

text.p: Brent paper firmed again on Friday, short-dated swaps gaining as much as six cents from early trade amid talk of more early May crude moving out of northwest Europe, traders said.
June Brent was 30 cents firmer at $17.99 a barrel by 1500 GMT, lifted by strength on heating fuel markets in the U.S., where a northeastern states are experiencing a spring cold snap.

Brent CFDs for April 21-25 gained about six cents to talk at June Brent -46/-43 cents after an early deal at -50 cents, helped by talk that early May Brent cargoes may be heading into the Mediterranean.
"There's unconfirmed talk that a VLCC of Brent will be moving to Croatia's Rijeka refinery," said a trader.
"There's physical demand for Brent at (May) -40 cents - that's a pretty good bid," he said.
Shipping brokers said China's Sinochem fixed the VLCC Harrier to take four cargoes of Brent Blend loading at Sullom Voe to Rijeka, where it has a processing arrangement.
Traders said the possibility of North Sea barrels finding homes in the U.S. Gulf left uncovered by recent heavy West African sales to Asia was also helping to lift spot market sentiment.
Japanese, South Korean and Chinese buyers have all been active on the West African market this week, picking up May cargoes of Nigerian and Angolan crudes.

Traders said spot differentials were still firming up as a result. A Bonny Light cargo traded at Dated Brent +35/+36 cents on Thursday, Qua Iboe at Dated Brent +31 cents and an Escravos at Dated Brent +16/+17 cents.

"Hopefully this upbeat (mood) will continue until next week. Of course, a lot of the April stuff is soon going to be on the water, mostly heading for the U.S., unless it gets diverted to the Far East which of course can happen," one seller said.
"I think interest in the Far East, Japan, Korea, Singapore and China, is picking up for West African grades," a European lifter said.

Negotiations continued between Algeria's Sonatrach and term lifters over May prices, with the state company "targeting something in the (Dated Brent plus) 50s for Saharan Blend," a European lifter said.
Sellers of Russian Urals were trying to stick to current levels of about Dated Brent -$1.15 but buyers were seeking lower prices, expecting cheaper May alternatives to exert pressure.
